mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 3% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% MoM does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% MoM signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO drop > 2% MoM does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 5% and rising CPI does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or sustained PAYEMS increase does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and real personal savings (RSAFS) increase by more than 5% MoM, it signals a contraction in consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and RSAFS increases > 5% MoM
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of declining HOUST and increasing RSAFS does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals accommodative monetary policy in a tight labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with tight labor market
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and low UNRATE does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation < 0.1).
